articles.title: Brandy and Monica Announce ‘The Boy Is Mine’ 2027 Residency at Las Vegas’ Resorts World
articles.summary: Brandy and Monica have announced “The Boy Is Mine Vegas Residency,” their first-ever series of shows in Las Vegas. The R&B icons announced the residency following a performance of their collaborative hit “The Boy Is Mine” on “Dancing With the Stars” during its Grammy-themed episode on Tuesday…
body: Produced by the Black Promoters Collective, the residency comes following their sold-out “The Boy Is Mine” tour, which saw each artist trading off to perform hits and deep cuts from their respective catalogs. Following the conclusion of the tour in December 2025, Brandy and Monica continued to perform together at the St. Lucia Jazz & Arts Festival and a co-headlining performance at the 2026 Essence Festival of Culture. Read Variety ‘s review of Brandy and Monica’s Los Angeles tour stop here.

“BPC is proud to be working with Brandy and Monica again,” says Shelby Joyner, President of Black Promoters Collective, in a statement. “We saw on The Boy Is Mine tour how much it meant to fans to see them share a stage, and I’m excited to build on what we created together. Bringing The Boy Is Mine to Las Vegas as Black Promoters Collective’s first residency is a big moment for us. We’ve built BPC by betting on artists we believe in and listening to their fans. This residency takes that work into a new arena for our company, and I can’t think of two artists I’d rather take that step with.”

articles.summary: Brenda Song recently revealed that she felt she was “overworked” and “underpaid” while starring on “The Suite Life of Zack and Cody.” The “Running Point” actress opened up about her experience working on the Disney Channel sitcom while appearing on her former co-star Dylan Sprouse’s and co-host…
body: Song did admit that she passed out on set once while filming a scene that called for a hot tub, which malfunctioned and was heated to “250 degrees,” said Sprouse. “I remember just breathing really heavy, and my chest felt really hot. I just went, ‘Am I having a panic attack?’ And then all of a sudden I remember stars and gone.”

She continued: “I think the only thing that was hard about that time was I feel like we were underpaid and overworked. But Disney did give us a platform to be sitting here right now. So it’s very hard to complain about certain things.”

Earlier this month, Sprouse also touched on how the show was “extremely underfunded,” despite being “popular” on his podcast. “In terms of the channel higher-ups, we were also kind of weirdly the ugly duckling,” Sprouse said, before adding that “the only residual check I’ve ever received for ‘The Suite Life’ at all was a crossover episode with ‘Hannah Montana’ for five cents. I’m not joking,” he said. “Imagine that. In a time where residuals would have been great,” Sprouse added, “Not a single paycheck for being arguably one of the most popular shows.”

articles.title: Stacy Keach, Star of ‘Mike Hammer,’ ‘Fat City,’ Dies at 85
articles.summary: Stacy Keach, a commanding actor whose work includes movies like “Fat City” and the starring role in “The New Mike Hammer” series on CBS, died Tuesday in Poland. He was 85. His wife, Małgosia Tomassi, confirmed his death to Variety.
body: “Stacy was not only a legendary actor, admired and loved by audiences the world over, but also my beloved husband, my companion and the heart of our family,” the statement said. “His passing leaves an immeasurable emptiness in our lives. But his extraordinary spirit, his unforgettable voice and the love he gave so generously will remain with us forever.

Active on stage, film and TV into his eighties, he popped up in “ The Bourne Legacy,” “Nebraska,” “Two and a Half Men,” “Ray Donovan” and had a recurring voice role on “The Simpsons.” Keach was also known for playing Cardinal Kevin Kearns on “Blue Bloods.” His TV appearances included “Man With a Plan” and “The Black List.” His final role was in “Jay Kelly” in 2025, as the father of Jay Kelly, played by George Clooney.
In 2010, he received a Helen Hayes award for his performance of “King Lear,” for Shakespeare Theater Co., one of many stage honors over the course of his career.

articles.title: Tinto Brass obituary
articles.summary: Italian director drawn to the erotic best known for his 1979 film Caligula, which is now regarded as a cult favourite. No matter how one defines the films of the director Tinto Brass, who has died aged 93, they manage, in most cases, to keep a distance, however narrowly, from pornography.
body: There is no doubt that most of his two dozen features, the most notorious being Salon Kitty (1976) and Caligula (1979), could be variously labelled sexploitation (the female nude shown purely for sexual or commercial reasons), sexist, softcore (no erections or ejaculations), kitsch (bad taste) and camp (“its essence being its love of the unnatural: of artifice and exaggeration”, in Susan Sontag ’s definition).

If a director who has a personal stamp, and whose oeuvre has a thematic and stylistic consistency, is considered an auteur, then Brass, who wrote and edited his own films, would qualify. Needless to say, he was in a different category from Federico Fellini, whom he idolised; Luchino Visconti, whom he parodied; and Roberto Rossellini, for whom he was assistant on two films. Yet, in the early 1960s, Brass was thought of as one of the most interesting directors of the new generation.

articles.title: David Walliams accused of sexual misconduct after losing injunction bid
articles.summary: ITN and the Guardian allege the comedian preyed on teenage girls and young women. He has denied all allegations.
body: ITV News and the Guardian have published reports alleging that David Walliams has been accused of sexual misconduct by several women, including one who was aged 15.

The allegations were made as a part of a joint three-year investigation, external by the two news organisations, which was published after the entertainer lost a legal bid to stop the claims against him being made public.
Some of the women accuse Walliams of "grooming" them when they were teenagers. One now characterises her alleged encounter with Walliams at 15 years old as a "sexual assault".
In a letter to journalists published by the Guardian, Walliams said he was "not a sexual predator" and had not "broken the law".

articles.title: VisionQuest: The Identity Of The Client, Explained
articles.summary: At long last, VisionQuest has revealed who, exactly, The Client is, and they're basically a proxy for a different character from Marvel's comics.
body: Ultron (James Spader) may have no strings on him anymore, but someone has been manipulating the events of "VisionQuest" like a puppetmaster. That someone is The Client, who hired the bounty hunter Paladin (Todd Stashwick) to capture Vision (Paul Bettany). We've gotten glimpses of The Client all season, but only as a digitally altered voice or a faceless avatar... until Episode 7, "Immolation."
At the episode's end, Vision and Ultron's gynoid lover Jocasta (T'Nia Miller) are delivered to The Client's doorstep. Out of said door walks... someone who looks just like Ultron's human avatar. Huh?

"Forever" clarifies it. "The Client" is Virgil Horton, grandson of Phineas Horton (Bettany), the scientist who created the Synthetic Man/Human Torch (Bettany again) in the 1940s. As Virgil explains, the Synthetic Man's uncontrolled fire powers mean that Dr. Horton was considered a failure. Years ago, Virgil joined with Dr. Josephine Carrington (Miller) to perfect AI in hopes of redeeming the Horton family legacy. They scanned their own brainwaves to create the genesis of what Tony Stark (Robert Downey Jr.) completed.

articles.title: ‘I’m looking for faces which surprise me’: how Richard Avedon photographed the soul of his subjects
articles.summary: Ron Howard’s illuminating Netflix documentary looks back on the career of one of America’s most inventive and versatile photographers. Richard Avedon had only taken a couple of frames when he accidentally hit his head on a light being held above him. The Dalai Lama burst into laughter.
body: Avedon’s assistant, Sebastian Kim, was baffled. “I was like, what the hell happened? There’s only four frames out of a roll of 12 frames,” he recalls in a phone interview. “I realised he knew at that moment that something had happened, a mistake had happened: he hit his head and the Dalai Lama lit up.”

Kim, 52, now an eminent photographer in his own right, is among the interviewees who feature in a new documentary, Avedon, directed by Oscar winner Ron Howard, which premiered at the Cannes film festival and is released on Netflix this week.

The film explores the six-decade career of the fashion and portrait photographer renowned for white backgrounds that stripped away distractions and for capturing figures ranging from Marilyn Monroe and Charlie Chaplin to civil rights activists, anti-war protesters and working-class Americans.

Avedon was raised in New York City. His father, Jacob Avedon, co-founded a specialty store on Fifth Avenue, which was lost overnight during the Great Depression. Avedon struggled academically, flunking out of high school despite winning a citywide poetry prize.

articles.title: Does Marvel's VisionQuest Have A Post-Credits Scene? A Spoiler-Free Guide
articles.summary: We're here to tell you, in a completely spoiler-free way, whether the finale episode of Marvel Studios' VisionQuest TV show contains any post-credits scenes.
body: The end of a trilogy that started back in 2020 is upon us. The "WandaVision" trilogy is one of the most significant pieces of Marvel's Multiverse Saga, focusing on Wanda Maximoff and Vision's complicated relationship and the characters who are connected to them. With "VisionQuest" reaching its conclusion, the trilogy has been capped off. But is it all over once the credits start to roll on the final episode? Or is there more to it?

This series brings back Paul Bettany as Vision for what is presumably one last ride. It also brings back James Spader as Ultron more than a decade later. How exactly is Ultron alive in "VisionQuest?" That's one of many questions the show has answered during its run.

The Marvel Cinematic Universe is notorious for including post-credits scenes in its movies and TV shows. Some of them have been very good and consequential, such as Thanos arriving in "The Avengers." Some of Marvel's worst post-credits scenes? Not so good. Whatever shape they take, it's always reasonable to wonder whether or not a given MCU project contains a credits scene or two.

articles.title: Stacy Keach, Who Played Badasses With the Best of Them, Dies at 85
articles.summary: He was a memorable Mike Hammer, starred in 'Fat City,' 'The New Centurions' and in Cheech & Chong films and excelled at Shakespeare on the stage.
body: Stacy Keach, the two-fisted actor who starred as the hard-boiled private eye Mike Hammer on television and won acclaim — but never superstardom — for his work in Fat City, The New Centurions and many other films, died Tuesday. He was 85.
Keach died at his family home in Magdalenka, Poland, his fourth wife, Malgosia Tomassi Keach, announced.

“Stacy was not only a legendary actor, admired and loved by audiences the world over, but also my beloved husband, my companion and the heart of our family. His passing leaves an immeasurable emptiness in our lives. But his extraordinary spirit, his unforgettable voice and the love he gave so generously will remain with us forever.”

Keach was regarded as perhaps the best American Shakespearean actor of his era; in the early 1970s, the influential New York Times critic Clive Barnes called him “one of the great Hamlets of our time” and “the finest American classic actor since John Barrymore.”

articles.title: Cerys Matthews pays tribute to her family as she receives OBE
articles.summary: Matthews was behind the Welsh rock band Catatonia who shot to fame during the "Cool Cymru" movement of the 1990s.
body: Singer and presenter Cerys Matthews paid tribute to her family as she received an OBE.
Matthews, from Cardiff, was appointed an Officer of the Order of the British Empire (OBE) for services to music and received a medal from the Prince of Wales.
Speaking after the ceremony, Matthews said she accepted the OBE in memory of her family and "in gratitude of the freedoms I have as a female in this era".
Matthews' voice is also familiar to many over her Christmas holidays because of her 1999 rendition of Baby It's Cold Outside, sung with Sir Tom Jones.
